I've farmed this land for 30 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. Let me think through each crop.

My 19.1 mu — I'll put about 15 mu in the wheat-maize rotation like always, and keep 4.1 mu for cotton on the sandier piece that doesn't do as well for grain. Cotton needs that lighter soil anyway.

**Wheat (winter, 15 mu):** Last year I got about 480 kg/mu, decent year. I'll sow Jimai improved variety around early October after the maize comes off. Base fertilizer I'll put 2 bags of compound (that's about 40 kg per bag, 15-15-15) per mu before ploughing, then topdress urea at greening in March. That gives me roughly 27 kg N, 10 kg P, 8 kg K per mu. Well water irrigation — I'll water before winter (dongshui), then at greening, jointing, and grain filling. Four waterings. Spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually 2-3 times. I plough after maize harvest since wheat needs a proper seedbed.

**Maize (summer, 15 mu):** Straight after wheat harvest in June. I use Zhengdan hybrid seed — neighbor got 620 kg/mu with it. No-till, just direct seed into the wheat stubble, saves time and diesel. One bag compound at sowing, then urea topdress at big trumpet stage — around 28 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Irrigate twice if the rain is poor, maybe once if July rains come. Spray once or twice for corn borer.

**Cotton (spring, 4.1 mu):** Cotton is more work but the price can be good. Plant late April after ploughing. Improved variety (Lumianyan). Fertilizer lower than grain — about 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K per mu, most as base with some topdressing at flowering. Irrigate 3 times through the season. Cotton needs many sprays — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I usually spray 6 times. Expect around 230 kg seed cotton per mu.

My fertilizer rates come from long habit: two bags compound as base plus urea topdressing, a little extra N to be safe because losing yield hurts far more than spending a few extra yuan on urea.
